title: Servicing Manual, Chapter on Payment Plans for Deficiency Balance Accounts
content:
**1. Authorisation.** A payment plan on an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts starts only under an arrangement offer of the payment-plan type that the borrower has accepted, as the offer record shows.

**2. Acceptance period.** The plan offer must be accepted no later than the band's plan-offer period after it was made. The acceptance period is counted in calendar days from the offer date, and an acceptance on the last day is in time; an offer not accepted in time expires.

**3. Eligibility of the balance.** A plan is offered only on an open account with a balance of at least the band's smallest balance eligible for a monthly plan; a smaller balance may be spread over no more than the band's small-balance number of monthly installments of equal amount.

**4. Installment and term.** The monthly installment is the greater of the minimum monthly plan installment and the minimum percent of the balance on the acceptance date, rounded up to the cent. *This clause is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis for the monthly installment of a plan.* The number of installments is the balance divided by the installment rounded up, never more than the band's maximum number of monthly plan installments; the first installment is due no more than the band's first-installment period after acceptance on a due day within the band's due-day range, and later installments follow monthly.

**5. After a broken arrangement.** Where the account had a broken arrangement in the rolling 12 months (at least one), a new plan also requires a down payment of the band's restart down payment percentage of the balance. *This clause is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis for the restart down payment.* Once broken arrangements in the rolling 12 months reach the band's limit on broken arrangements, no new plan is offered.

**6. Breaking.** A plan is broken when an installment remains unpaid the band's grace period after its due date; the account returns to open and keeps every payment already made.

## Acceptance period, boundary cases (hypothetical)

With a 14-day acceptance period and an offer made on the 1st of a month:

| Acceptance on | In time? |
|---|---|
| The 14th | Yes |
| The 15th (the last day) | Yes |
| The 16th | No; the offer has expired |

## Points of judgement

| Fact on the account | Clause in force |
|---|---|
| Account not open | No plan is offered |
| Balance below the smallest eligible balance | No monthly plan; the balance may be spread over at most the small-balance number of equal monthly installments |
| Broken arrangements in the rolling 12 months at the band's limit | No new plan is offered |
| Installment unpaid at the end of the grace period | The plan is broken; the account returns to open with all payments kept |

The rolling 12 months is the period ending today that runs back to the same calendar day 12 months earlier, that day excluded (the last day of the month where that day does not exist).

superseded_clauses: The monthly installment is the greater of plan_min_monthly_payment_usd and plan_min_payment_pct_of_balance of the balance on the acceptance date, rounded up to the cent

Where the account had a broken arrangement in the rolling 12 months (deficiency_msr_broken_arrangements_12m at least 1), a new plan also requires a down payment of plan_restart_down_payment_pct of the balance
